hints: Focus on what a single ester group tells you about the number of oxygen atoms in one molecule of X.
Use the 27.6% oxygen by mass to work out the total $M_r$ of X, remembering the mass of two O atoms is 32.
For each alcohol plus acid pair, find the ester $M_r$ using $M_r(ester) = M_r(alcohol) + M_r(acid) - 18$ and see which matches your value near 116.
walkthrough:
**Count the oxygens in the ester**

Every ester group, $\text{-COO-}$, contains exactly 2 oxygen atoms. Since X has a single ester group, one molecule of X contains 2 O atoms.

Mass of oxygen per mole of X:
$$m(\text{O}) = 2 \times 16.0 = 32.0 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$$

**Find the $M_r$ of X from percentage**

The 32.0 g of oxygen is 27.6% of the total mass. Let $M_r$ be the relative molecular mass of X.

$$\frac{32.0}{M_r} \times 100 = 27.6$$
$$M_r = \frac{32.0 \times 100}{27.6} \approx 115.9$$

**Link hydrolysis products to ester mass**

Ester hydrolysis is the reverse of esterification:
$$\text{ester} + \text{water} \rightarrow \text{alcohol} + \text{carboxylic acid}$$
So by mass conservation:
$$M_r(\text{ester}) = M_r(\text{alcohol}) + M_r(\text{acid}) - M_r(\text{H}_2\text{O})$$
$$M_r(\text{ester}) = M_r(\text{alcohol}) + M_r(\text{acid}) - 18$$

**Test the butan-1-ol and ethanoic acid pair**

Butan-1-ol, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$, has $M_r = 74$. Ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, has $M_r = 60$.

$$M_r = 74 + 60 - 18 = 116$$
This matches the 115.9 calculated from the oxygen percentage, so this pair is possible.

options.A: Butan-1-ol ($M_r$ = 74) + ethanoic acid ($M_r$ = 60) gives an ester of $M_r$ = 74 + 60 - 18 = 116. Oxygen % = 32/116 x 100 = 27.6%, exactly matching the data. This is butyl ethanoate.
options.B: Ethanol ($M_r$ = 46) + propanoic acid ($M_r$ = 74) gives an ester of $M_r$ = 46 + 74 - 18 = 102. Oxygen % = 32/102 x 100 = 31.4%, which is too high. Trap is guessing without calculating $M_r$.
options.C: Methanol ($M_r$ = 32) + methanoic acid ($M_r$ = 46) gives an ester of $M_r$ = 32 + 46 - 18 = 60. Oxygen % = 32/60 x 100 = 53.3%, far too high. This is the smallest possible ester, so its oxygen percentage is the largest.
options.D: Propan-2-ol ($M_r$ = 60) + butanoic acid ($M_r$ = 88) gives an ester of $M_r$ = 60 + 88 - 18 = 130. Oxygen % = 32/130 x 100 = 24.6%, which is too low. Larger esters have lower oxygen percentages.
